extracted.intended_audience: Python developers, educators, and creators producing mathematical animations with the Manim Community library
extracted.subtask_description: Authoring Scene classes and animations using the Manim Community Python library (constructing mobjects, arranging/layout, and applying animated transforms). Includes practical examples and usage idioms from the docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Tex/MathTex for LaTeX text and math
rubrics_metrics.description: Instantiate LaTeX-rendered text with Tex(...) and mathematical expressions with MathTex(...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show title = Tex(r"This is some \LaTeX") and basel = MathTex(r"\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{6}"). Use Tex for general LaTeX text and MathTex for inline/display math so equations render correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group and arrange mobjects before animating
rubrics_metrics.description: Use VGroup(...) to combine mobjects and call arrange(...) to set layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: VGroup(title, basel).arrange(DOWN) — arrange groups prior to playing animations so relative positions are correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer built-in animation constructors for transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use animations such as Write, FadeIn, FadeOut, Transform, Create, ApplyPointwiseFunction, LaggedStart to animate mobjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Write(title), FadeIn(basel, shift=DOWN), Transform(title, transform_title), Create(grid, run_time=3, lag_ratio=0.1), ApplyPointwiseFunction(...), and Transform(square, circle). These provide standard, composable visual transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control layering/order by the order of self.add(...)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add mobjects to the scene in an order that enforces desired z-order (what appears on top).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example comment: self.add(grid, grid_title)  # Make sure title is on top of grid. Adding the title after the grid ensures it is rendered above the grid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare objects before non-linear transforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Call preparation routines on mobjects that will be transformed non-linearly before applying the transform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: grid.prepare_for_nonlinear_transform() is called before grid.animate.apply_function(...). Some objects need preparation so subsequent pointwise/nonlinear transforms preserve appearance and anchors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pointwise/apply_function for geometric/nonlinear effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Animate an object's points with ApplyPointwiseFunction or .animate.apply_function to produce nonlinear deformations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ApplyPointwiseFunction(lambda point: complex_to_R3(np.exp(R3_to_complex(point))), square) and grid.animate.apply_function(lambda p: p + np.array([np.sin(p[1]), np.sin(p[0]), 0])). Use these to implement complex coordinate mappings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use StreamLines for continuous motion and control warm-up/flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct StreamLines with a vector field and start the animation with control over warm_up and flow_speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: stream_lines = StreamLines(func, stroke_width=2, max_anchors_per_line=30); stream_lines.start_animation(warm_up=False, flow_speed=1.5); self.wait(stream_lines.virtual_time / stream_lines.flow_speed). Use warm_up and flow_speed to tune appearance and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose staggered animations with LaggedStart and generator expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use LaggedStart to run a sequence of animations with delays between them; generator expressions can create per-object animations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: LaggedStart(*(FadeOut(obj, shift=DOWN) for obj in basel)). Useful for fading out many objects in a staggered fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set fill and opacity to control visual emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use set_fill(color, opacity=...) on shapes for color and transparency control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: circle.set_fill(PINK, opacity=0.5) — semi-transparent fills can highlight or de-emphasize shapes during animation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use geometric primitives and helper classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage built-in classes such as Square, Circle, NumberPlane, and helper transforms (flip, rotate) as building blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show Square(), Circle(), NumberPlane(), square.flip(RIGHT), square.rotate(-3 * TAU / 8). Using primitives simplifies scene construction and composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project/community expectations and license
rubrics_metrics.description: Manim Community is free and open-source and is permissively released under the MIT license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The docs state: 'Manim is a free and open-source project ... permissively released under the MIT license.' The site also encourages contributing (Contribute to Manim, Submit a Bug, Translate) and links to code of conduct and community channels (GitHub, Discord, Reddit).
